articles.title: GTA 6: Release date, how much it is and everything you need to know
articles.summary: A new launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI reveals more details about what's set to be the biggest game of the year.
articles.body:
Rockstar has released a new launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, revealing more details about what is set to be the biggest game of the year.

GTA 6 became available to pre-order at midnight on 25 June in the UK and elsewhere around the world, after Rockstar revealed the game's pre-sales launch date and cover art in mid-June.

Analysts believe Rockstar's action adventure could become the most expensive game ever made, with estimates putting development costs at more than $1bn (£866m).

Here's what we do and don't know about GTA 6 so far.

The new launch trailer again confirmed GTA 6 will be released on 19 November.

Suggesting no further delays to its release, the video gave fans a glimpse into the missions that protagonists Jason and Lucia will take part in.

It also featured a new song from French electronic music artists Justice, who were revealed to be the game's original score composers.

The game has been previously delayed twice , from autumn 2025 and May 2026.

In a statement when the second delay was announced, Rockstar said it needed extra months to finish the game with the level of polish fans had come to "expect and deserve".

Rockstar said players who pre-order will be able to begin pre-loading it on their consoles on 12 November to ensure they are able to play at launch.

How much will GTA 6 cost and what can I play it on?

The sixth game in the main series will be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.

There's no news on when a PC version will be released - it's also currently unknown whether it will come to Nintendo Switch 2.

The game will cost £69.99 in the UK and $79.99 in the US - with an ultimate edition, featuring extra vehicles and weapons, priced at £89.99 and $99.99, respectively.

Physical copies of the game will contain a code for a digital download for the game inside a box, rather than a disc.

Rockstar has not yet confirmed whether an updated online mode will be released as soon as GTA 6 launches.

The game's PlayStation Store listing currently states "Grand Theft Auto VI is a single-player experience" - implying there will be no online mode at launch. But given GTA Online's success , it will likely exist at some point.

How any future age verification legislation in the UK around social media and particularly messaging in gaming could therefore affect it, if at all, is still unknown.

GTA 6 will cost $80 - and physical edition will not contain a disc

What we know after the big Grand Theft Auto 6 preview

What is GTA 6 about, where is it set and who are its main characters?

GTA 6 will feature its first ever playable female protagonist in a 3D setting - Lucia - alongside her partner in life and crime, Jason, as a second playable character.

From what we've seen in two gameplay trailers and Netflix's extended look , the story will follow the pair in a Bonnie and Clyde-esque adventure through the seedy underbelly of America after an " easy score goes wrong ".

Like other GTA games before it, the sixth chapter is set in a fictional US state - this time in Leonida, which is Rockstar's version of Florida.

Fans of previous games will be excited to hear that Vice City, which is inspired by Miami, will return, featuring as the main city within the state.

GTA 6's cover art revealed by Rockstar on 18 June made several nods to the setting with alligators and flamingos.

Rockstar Games breaks silence on Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks

How long has Rockstar taken to make GTA 6?

It's no secret that GTA 6 has been a few years in the making.

The franchise's last instalment, GTA 5, was released in September 2013 - and quickly became one of the best-selling games of all time.

It's unclear whether Rockstar has been working on the sixth instalment for all of that time, however, as in 2018 it also released another huge sequel - Red Dead Redemption 2.

Rockstar confirmed for the first time that it was working on a sixth game in the series in February 2022.

The rising cost of development and immense pressure to live up to the series' hype are all contributing factors as to why gamers have had to wait so long for the game's release.

Several months later, footage and images leaked after teenage hackers targeted the company .

It has also seen some issues since, including accusations of "union-busting" by sacked workers at Rockstar North , its Edinburgh HQ, where developers have been racing to get GTA 6 ready for release in November.

Grand Theft Auto boss denies trying to keep tabs on union membership

Why is there so much excitement about it?

To put it simply, the GTA franchise is one of the biggest and most profitable entertainment properties in history.

GTA 5 has sold nearly 230 million copies, making it one of the best-selling games of all time - which has generated billions of dollars in revenue for Rockstar.

The game's sandbox gameplay, where players can explore vast open worlds with considerable freedom - sometimes controversially - has seen it be continuously lauded as the ultimate expression for what the interactive medium can do.

Freelance video games journalist Vic Hood said each entry in the series "continued to push technical and gameplay boundaries", with GTA Online helping to "pioneer the live service model as we know it".

She added that the games were also "extremely culturally relevant" too.

"Rockstar has always had its finger on the pulse of music, entertainment, societal, political, celebrity, and online culture trends, and they've never shied away from satirising these things in GTA games," she said.

British gaming entrepreneur Sir Ian Livingstone told the BBC's Today programme that the series, originally developed in Scotland, was "bigger than any film or song" and an "incredible achievement in interactive software".

Speculation as to how a sixth game can top even the gigantic heights of its predecessor has meant that any latest news, no matter how small, has been met with a flurry of hype and excitement.

Both of GTA 6's previous gameplay trailers currently have a total of roughly 447 million views combined.

articles.title: Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes Documentary You Can See Everything Conjures Sympathy for the Devil
articles.summary: You Can See Everything review: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim conjure sympathy for the devil.
articles.body:
You Can See Everything is in theaters October 15.

At nearly three hours in length, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s You Can See Everything is a staggering, unnerving documentary about Silicon Valley and whether you can truly know someone. Its focus is Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, who granted the filmmakers unprecedented access for about a month before her prison stint began in 2023. However, the movie is as much about the question of Holmes’ culpability as it is about cults of personality and cultural mythologies at large — not to mention Fielder’s own oeuvre and TV persona as the creator of shows like The Rehearsal, a prankish work of obsession laced with hidden sincerity.

The total here feels greater than the sum of its parts, owing to the allure of its eerie filmmaking and the sheer brain-breaking scope of its ambition as a work of haunting, self-reflexive cinema. Filled with suffocating 4:3 close-ups shot with long lenses, and awash in shadow to disguise motive, the movie’s rapturous form feels like the product of invasive surveillance amidst a mile-a-minute chase. This is despite the fact that most of it is composed of simple, static conversations — a magnificent sleight of hand.

It initially unfolds at a beachside home in San Diego rented by Holmes and her husband, the wild-eyed hotel heir Billy Evans, a man seen voraciously absorbing audio material at double speed. We’re reintroduced to Holmes’ story by way of news clips scoring footage of her daily life, a sort of “previously on” segment detailing her conviction for fraud. However, as an anchor utters the phrase “pathological liar,” the camera falls on Fielder for the first time as he appears like a poltergeist in the corner.

The hilarity of Fielder’s awkward, lumbering presence in this domestic setting — headphones at the ready around his neck like he’s playing the role of “a director” — clashes wildly with unsettling zooms into empty spaces and people’s expressions. As Holmes and Evans raise their two young children, Fielder probes the couple through intimate sit-downs on their couch, and conversations in passing wherever he can steal them.

With the saturation turned up to the edge of uncanniness — in concert with Oppenheim’s Chris Hansen drama from this year, Primetime — Holmes’ deep blue eyes become Fielder’s greatest challenge yet, as a man seemingly taken by her charm while also thoroughly unconvinced of her claims that she did nothing wrong. And yet, when it comes to her seemingly magical, test-for-any-disease device, he extends her an enormous benefit of doubt, if only to keep unspooling a tightly-wound thread, thus allowing Holmes and Evans to hoist themselves with their own petards.

As Fielder grows more entwined with the couple, it’s hard not to see the Nathan For You host as if he’s peering into a mirror of sorts. Holmes is a fellow manipulator, though perhaps she’s more adept at it than Fielder is. Fielder’s TV character is that of a slightly naïve and self-effacing man who secretly nudges his subjects in a particular direction through suggestion. But while his goal is entertainment, Holmes’ is securing financial investment, something she continues to work on even as her prison sentence looms.

The visual framing creates a proximity and palpable tension between Fielder and Holmes, but it crafts an equally compelling portrait of Evans as a man potentially pulling the strings. However, the question of whether Holmes is letting him do this or if she’s even aware of what he’s up to remains a central point of inquiry. It’s rare to watch a documentary that gradually becomes about its own making and finances, but these are among its most exhilarating developments; You Can See Everything really does want you to witness its every dimension.

You might find yourself asking why the film occupies such an enormous runtime, but the answer becomes self-evident once it moves into its second half. The question of who Holmes truly is — A deceiver in denial? Someone in the throes of delusion? — remains hauntingly open-ended. This not only imbues the film with a debilitating uncertainty about the kinds of tech moguls running our lives, but it also forces Fielder to turn to a very surprising ally for an alternative peek into Holmes’ mind.

Then again, perhaps this person’s identity is not so surprising if you’re familiar with cultural depictions of Holmes and Fielder’s usual M.O. But the film remains remarkably unpredictable by creating circumstances where people are forced to watch and reflect rather uncomfortably on transcripts and existing footage. Bit by bit, this aforementioned celebrity becomes a kind of co-conspirator in Fielder’s audit of the truth through inviting fireside chats that reveal the gradual frustrations of this particular journey.

As the questions about Holmes and Evans grow more labyrinthine, the movie becomes an astonishing mise en abyme (story within a story) by way of Rehearsal-like re-enactments. These are aimed not only at filling in the gaps caused by Holmes’ incarceration but at using cinematic tools to mine for all possible truths at once to see which one fits… if any at all. It’s exactly the kind of thing you’d expect from Fielder’s experiments, and yet it remains shocking at every turn. At some points, it becomes hard to believe the things you’re seeing and hearing were captured in the first place.

The possibility of the production itself falling apart through the sudden revocation of access always looms, and it certainly isn’t helped by the fact that Fielder is at his most confrontational as an on-screen personality. His provocations are in service of a deeply human search for not only who Holmes is but why she is — a mystery that only grows more confounding the more we learn about her, and the closer Fielder gets to her. It’s a sympathetic look at a person who, despite the harm she’s caused, seems hell-bent on staying the course and re-enacting the past… not unlike Fielder himself.

The result is wildly captivating, woven from creeping close-ups and stealthy investigations into the kind of minds making modern tech industries tick. It’s one of the most electric and enrapturing films you’re likely to see this year, and by the time it concludes, its gargantuan 174 minutes may not feel like enough.

articles.title: Sony Reminds PlayStation Plus Subscribers That GTA 5 Leaves the Library 2 Days Before GTA 6 Comes Out
articles.summary: PS5 and PS4 players taking advantage of PS Plus to play GTA 5 and GTA Online better get their hours in because their days are numbered. GTA 5 is being removed from the PS Plus catalogue just two days before GTA 6’s launch in November.
articles.body:
PS5 and PS4 players taking advantage of PS Plus to play GTA 5 and GTA Online better get their hours in because their days are numbered. GTA 5 is being removed from the PS Plus catalogue just two days before GTA 6’s launch in November.

GTA 5 has sold an eye-watering 230 million copies since its 2013 launch, so you'd imagine most who are interested in experiencing Rockstar’s sweeping and beautiful take on Los Angeles have already done so. But if you’re one of the few who hasn't, you have until November 17 to get it done via PS Plus.

Sony has been warning PS5 players about the change. “If you’re counting down the days until GTA 6 arrives on PS5 on November 19, why not take a trip to Los Santos in the meantime?” the message said .

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

“GTA 5 is available to play in the Game Catalog for PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium members, but only until November 17. So whether you’ve yet to experience the tale of Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, or want to revisit it before Jason and Lucia’s Vice City story begins, now’s the time.”

The popup was followed by a prompt to preorder GTA 6 . It’s just another example of how huge Rockstar’s sequel will be, and what an impact it will have on game sales for platform holders like Sony.

Expected to be the most expensive video game of all time , GTA 6 is likely to make that money back fairly quickly. Even actors like Game of Thrones’ Kit Harington have said he’s excited for GTA 6 , despite not being a gamer.

Rockstar developers traveled across Florida on GTA 6 research trips to portray the state as authentically as possible in its satire-laden recreation of Miami and the surrounding areas. CBS news recently did a segment on GTA 6 , astonished by how accurately the game captures the city.

Elsewhere, the Australian government put out a graphic that informed citizens of their rights for requesting time off work when GTA 6 launches next month. In the meantime, Rockstar has been taking over Miami in its big marketing push leading up to launch.

But some Miami officials have expressed concern over the studio’s influence, with Rockstar promoting GTA 6 on the iconic Goodyear blimp, and collaborating with local NBA team the Miami Heat . There’s no stopping this train, which pulls into the station when GTA 6 launches for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.

articles.title: Trollheim: Gnomes Aims to Bring the Mystery and Whimsy of Nordic Folklore to a Survival Crafting Game
articles.summary: Trollheim: Gnomes, a new survival crafting game for PC based on Nordic folklore that IGN announced as part of IGN Fan Fest, comes from a team of ex-Mojang developers who all grew up playing in the Nordic woods and hearing folk tales of Sprýg Gnomes and other creatures and want to make a game about it. I got an early look at it, and there's one key thing that might set it apart in a very, very crowded genre: combat is optional.
articles.body:
Trollheim: Gnomes, a new survival crafting game for PC based on Nordic folklore that IGN announced as part of IGN Fan Fest, comes from a team of ex-Mojang developers who all grew up playing in the Nordic woods and hearing folk tales of Sprýg Gnomes and other creatures and want to make a game about it. I got an early look at it, and there's one key thing that might set it apart in a very, very crowded genre: combat is optional.

You'll gather building materials and as you level up, you'll be able to not only craft more and more intricate and complex structures, but you'll able to do so higher and higher up in the trees. It might be best thought of like living in a dark-forest version of a condo high-rise: the best unit is the penthouse. And you will run into opposition in the form of the Väsen, who are signficantly larger than your three-inch-tall gnome. All of that sounds pretty run-of-the-mill, right? But that's where the combat-optional hook comes in. The Väsen won't attack you on sight. They will if you antagonize them, but intriguingly, you can also befriend them by bringing them food or other items they need.

"If you want to hang out and make it cozy, that's up to you, said game director Jojje Dalunde. "You will always be able to achieve the same goals using a friendly approach as you would a hostile approach." Added studio founder Bjorne Larson, "We want combat to feel intentional. It's an opt-in. You will always know that you're stepping into something you might not be able to handle. You will be able to just enjoy your time with your friends and live the cozy experience of being this tiny Sprýg Gnome."

Adding to the cozy-if-you-want-it-to-be appeal of Trollheim are two welcome features: co-op and procedural generation. No matter how many people play with you (the max in one world is eight players), the Dark Forest – which the developers call a "main character" in Trollheim – will procedurally generate every time you start a new game, which should help the woods always feel new and mysterious.

But even if you don't opt in to combat, you'll still have to survive. Cold, wetness, and hunger are all very real threats to contend with. though your crafting extends beyond just housing. You can also make things like wingsuits to help you get around the Dark Forest more quickly and easily. You've got a single life bar to worry about that incorporates health and stamina into one meter for you to manage. I also saw some stealth elements in the hands-off demo I was presented, which made me happy to see.

Again, it won't be easy for Trollheim: Gnomes to stand out in the glut of its fellow survival crafting games. But the developers are, if nothing else, committed to building out their world. In addition to a Trollheim video game, they're constructing "an interconnected narrative that spans books, games, collectibles, film and lifestyle." The first of those transmedia experiences is a 288-page book available now called Trollheim: Tale of Sýstir. You can wishlist Trollheim: Gnomes on Steam if you're interested.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Humankind 2 Rethinks One of Its Predecessor’s Most Divisive Ideas
articles.summary: Humankind 2 takes a new approach to the monolithic cultures versus culture-switching debate, and could provide an elegant solution.
articles.body:
Switching cultures is no longer mandatory.

Your society is constructed of building blocks picked up along the way from multiple different cultures.

Nature plays a much larger role than it did in the first Humankind.

Historical 4X games tend to focus on a group of people you might call a nation, an empire, or indeed, a civilization. Amplitude's Humankind series is no different, but its upcoming second entry is looking at these concepts from a slightly different angle. After all, the idea of a shared identity comes from the stories we tell ourselves and each other about who we are as much as anything. And that is the starting point for charting a course through the ages in Humankind 2.

While the original Humankind and other staples of the genre typically begin with choosing a specific historical culture like the Greeks or the Egyptians, Humankind 2 is a bit different. The first choice you will make is between one of what I counted to be 19 different founding myths based on real-world oral traditions, each of which corresponds to at least one historical culture. This is the tale of how your people came to be, in their own minds.

We caught a glimpse of the Wild Twins origin, which gives bonuses for settling near wild animals and is associated with the Etruscans, and the Flood Tamers, which is ideally suited for fertile river valleys and is associated with the Ancient Egyptians. The hands-off demo we saw was using Humankind 2's new Historical Mode, which is set on a non-randomized map of Earth and placed each of these starter cultures in the region they are from in real life. Of course, this won't be the only way to play, with randomized worlds also being an option.

While the first Humankind shook up the genre by forcing you to pick a new culture in each of its six eras, a choice made even more controversial when it showed up in Civilization 7, Humankind 2 does not make this mandatory. It will have more than 70 cultures at launch spread out over the eras, but you can pick one at the very dawn of history and stick with it to the end. Each culture has an era or a set of eras in which it can be selected for the first time. Ancient Egypt, for example, can be selected in the first or second era. But if you already are that culture, you will never be forced to abandon it.

It may eventually make sense to do so for you. Amplitude mentioned you might get a choice to pick "a different culture associated with Egypt" in the later eras. But even keeping the "Ancient" Egyptians alive into modern times won't mean your culture stays completely static due to how you assemble a society out of different bonuses.

Each of the more than 70 cultures has their own specific customs tree to pull from. In the case of Ancient Egypt, this includes staples like Embalming, Hieroglyphics, and the office of the Pharaoh. These slot into what was, at least initially, 10 tradition slots that can be active at any one time. These can be pulled from any of the cultures you've played as throughout the run. So even if you choose to become the Carthaginians in the second era, you could keep the Pharaoh tradition active as long as you want.

There are even two special slots, called Legacies, which are rewards for completing a culture's tree. Each culture lets you pick one of two possible legacies to carry forward, which are more powerful than normal traditions. For Ancient Egypt, these are Scale of Eternity, which cements your people's legacy of monumental architecture, and Conquering Dynasty, which sets you on a path of military expansion in the name of the God-King.

So what does that mean for rulers who want to keep the same culture all game? Well, historical cultures are not the only way to gain new traditions. Another major source is Adaptations, which are earned based on where your civilization is located. An Egyptian player who settles in the desert will get access to different adaptations than one that settles in the Arctic, even though they will share the Ancient Egypt tradition tree in common. On top of this, you can also adopt a limited number of traditions from cultures you come into contact with through acculturation, allowing your society to keep advancing with the times based on what your neighbors are doing.

If you do want to pick a new culture at the start of a new era, there are a few more restrictions on that now than the original game's first-come, first-served free-for-all. You’ll initially get a choice of cultures with which yours have a real-world shared history. For Ancient Egypt, their natural progression for Era 2 is the Persians. Second, you can pick a culture with shared geography. If you're playing Ancient Egypt in their historical starting position, this includes the Berbers (also available as an Era 1 pick) or the Carthaginians. And finally, you can adopt the culture of another group you have come into contact with in the current era. We were shown Egypt able to become the Goths.

While you attempt to build a culture that can withstand the ages, Mother Earth herself won't be sitting idly by. Nature's role in history is seeing a renewed emphasis in Humankind 2, including mechanics for natural and human-caused climate change. We were shown, for example, that shifts in the global climate like the Medieval Warming Period or the Little Ice Age might cause whole biomes to shift in character. Plains regions which began as humid might suddenly become arid, changing their resource potentials and potentially leading to instability. Technology can begin to influence this in both directions in the later eras.

Aside from all this fresh flash, Humankind 2 looks like a fairly recognizable historical 4X game. We didn't get to dig too deep into the fine details of the mechanics, but the familiar resources of Money, Food, Production, Knowledge, Faith, and Authority were all visible in the UI. The stylized 3D map looks great, if a bit cramped on the Historical Earth version. Cities will dominate regions rather than acquiring individual tiles, like in most of Amplitude's other games. And elevation is still clearly visible.

Notably, in the demo we saw of Historical Mode, there were no empty regions by the end of Era 1. I was told the Neolithic phase is still part of the journey, but areas of the map you don't settle in right away will end up populated with their historical cultures fairly quickly, forcing you to expand by conquest or diplomacy rather than settling virgin fields.

Some other cultures we saw included the Romans and the Thule people of the prehistoric Arctic. Other Era 1 starting locations visible on the Historical Mode map, though we didn't get to see their names, included the Yucatan Peninsula, Northern Mexico, the American Great Lakes, Britain, Scandinavia, Southern France, Greece, the Carpathian Basin, West Africa, Central Africa, Mesopotamia, the Altai Mountains, the eastern shore of the Caspian Sea, and China's Yangtze River.

Cities seem to be following the "unpacked" model of most recent 4X games, sprawling across many tiles. A brief glimpse of modern Paris showed an urban footprint covering most of the region. I raised a concern about this since I don't particularly like it when the whole map is covered in buildings by the endgame. I prefer some areas to stay wild or rural in appearance to contrast the urban centers. And I was assured by Amplitude that there will be incentives not to blanket everything in concrete.

It's hard to say much about Humankind 2 without getting my own hands on it, of course. But from what little we were shown, I'm feeling pretty positive about the direction it's taking. Assembling a unique legacy from many cultural influences over the course of a campaign while still having the option to hold onto that core identity you started with seems like a shrewd solution to the debate between monolithic cultures and culture-switching. Giving nature a bigger part to play, I hope, will lead to more dynamic and memorable scenarios. And everything from monumental wonders to humble quarries looks slick and flavorful.

Humankind 2 is set to release on PC in 2027.

Leana Hafer is a contributing freelancer for IGN with a specialty in RPGs, strategy, horror, and survival games. She has been reviewing video games professionally since 2010 and is one of IGN's most prolific contributors, with more than 100 reviews published. You can also find her work on sites like PC Gamer and PCGamesN.

articles.title: With The Mummy 4 in Full Swing, Oded Fehr Jokes The Mummy 3 Doesn't Exist — Although John Hannah Firmly Disagrees
articles.summary: With The Mummy 4 currently shooting ahead of its October 15, 2027 release date, Oded Fehr, who reprises his role Ardeth Bay, joked that there were only two The Mummy movies released.
articles.body:
With The Mummy 4 currently shooting ahead of its October 15, 2027 release date, Oded Fehr, who reprises his role Ardeth Bay , joked that there were only two The Mummy movies released.

During a joint interview with John Hannah, who returns as Jonathan Carnahan in The Mummy 4, at Comic Con Holland , Fehr discussed what it feels like to once again play the all-action Ardeth Bay decades later. While talking about the experience, he dismissed the third The Mummy movie, subtitled Tomb of the Dragon Emperor — although Hannah clearly disagreed with the sentiment.

“It’s a very positive thing,” Fehr said of filming the originals. “The Mummy, The Mummy Returns — there wasn’t a third one — but the two movies were so… seriously, it was just fun.”

At this point, Hannah smirked and held three fingers up to the camera. He then mouthed, ‘There was a third movie.”

“No, there were two,” Fehr continued. “But, it’s a disagreement.”

While it looks like a bit of harmless banter between co-stars, Fehr’s comment taps into the sentiment around the franchise going into The Mummy 4, which will see Brendan Fraser reprising his iconic role as Rick O'Connell alongside Rachel Weisz as Evelyn O'Connell.

Weisz didn't appear in the divisive third entry (Maria Bello played the character instead), and many fans feel The Mummy 3 suffered as a result. Some fans have discounted it entirely, suggesting the events of The Mummy 3 shouldn’t be considered canon. In March, The Mummy 4 director duo Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett appeared to back that feeling up .

"Well, Rachel is in this one," Bettinelli-Olpin said when asked by Entertainment Weekly for a ruling on whether they considered Tomb of the Dragon Emperor to be canon.

"That should answer the question for you," Gillett then confirmed.

Oded Fehr didn’t feature in The Mummy 3, either, so you can perhaps understand his feelings on it. Hannah, though, appeared in all three The Mummy movies, which is perhaps why he defended The Mummy 3 in the interview.

There’s still much we don’t know about The Mummy 4 — even its final title is unannounced. But set photos have shown both Fraser and Weisz in character , in a setting that looks like 1950s post-war Britain.

articles.title: South Park Majorly Stumbles in Season 29, Episode 3 as the Series Tries to Lampoon Aura Farming and Looksmaxxing Culture
articles.summary: Talk about cringe. South Park delivers one of the weakest episodes in recent memory with "You Like That on Your Face."
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for South Park Season 29, Episode 3!

Yeesh, that was probably the weakest new episode of South Park in several years. As is often the case in the show's lesser moments, "You Like That on Your Face" has a few amusing gags and ideas, but none of it comes together as a cohesive whole. Talk about cringe...

This week, the series opts to turn its attention to Gen Z/Gen Alpha culture and hot-button issues like looksmaxxing and aura farming. Honestly, I was really hoping the opening scenes were meant to be a springboard to something else. Yes, aura farming is really stupid and laughable, but did we need an entire episode devoted to the practice?

In execution, "You Like That on Your Face" plays like a spiritual sequel to Season 8's "You Got F'd in the A," only with aura battles replacing the dance-offs of yore. Sadly, this episode compares very unfavorably to its predecessor. It hits too many of the same beats and doesn't really build on its ideas in a satisfying way. I don't know that "Hey, look how stupid and self-absorbed today's kids are" really makes for the greatest material.

This episode also leans way too heavily on the recurring gag of Sephora clerks squirting cream on children's faces and asking, "You like that on your face?" We get it. It's like porn, but with children. It's not particularly funny the first several times, and certainly not by the end when the twisted Sephora manager comes lumbering out of the darkness.

Again, there are some funny bits to be found in Episode 3. The initial reveal of the Sephora Backrooms is pretty funny (though this is another element that doesn't ultimately lead anywhere). The return of the Pet Semetary-spoofing Farmer Ted is also a welcome treat. And Randy himself getting into looksmaxxing and transforming himself into a 4th grader is probably the highlight of the episode. If anything, the South Park team really should have leaned more on that subplot. Randy can usually be counted upon to carry the series, at least when he's not hawking his Tegridy Farms wares. But I suppose we'll see if this particular development carries over into future episodes.

Clearly, despite the series' satirical title change, the intent with Season 29 is to pivot away from the politically focused Season 27/28 approach and return to a more classical brand of South Park that emphasizes the younger characters. That approach worked well enough in the first two episodes, but it falls pretty flat here. I don't know if South Park America strictly needs to go back to lampooning the Trump administration at every turn, but it does need to develop a more coherent overall storyline for the season and do a better job of tackling the more urgent topics of the day. This isn't it.

articles.title: GTA 6 Launch Trailer Teases Jason's Troubled Past, a Steamy Shower Scene With Lucia, and Much More
articles.summary: Rockstar has released the launch trailer for GTA 6, which shows us brand new footage of Jason and Lucia as well as the open world.
articles.body:
Rockstar has released the launch trailer for GTA 6 , which shows us brand new footage of Jason and Lucia as well as the open world.

The trailer, which weighs in at 1:30, touches on Jason's troubled past, which involved leaving the army not on the best of terms. We see snippets of a steamy shower scene with Lucia, who is wearing an ankle tag, and plenty of explosive open-world action.

Rather than showing gameplay, the launch trailer showcases cinematic action in GTA 6 as it nears its November 19 launch. As per Rockstar's partnership with Sony, the PS5 is prominent in the trailer, with the "plays best on PS5" message displayed at the start. The trailer confirms the footage was "captured on PS5."

The trailer begins with some narration from Jason. "I got in some trouble in the army," he begins. "Didn't leave on the best of terms. They don't give loans or anything to people like me." We see a bearded Jason working at Brian's Marina, buffing a boat before he receives a call from Lucia Caminos. Presumably this is the call Jason gets to pick up Lucia from prison.

We're shown what look like flashbacks to Jason's time in the army, where he appears to have been in the special forces. We see him wading through water as part of a military unit, and leaping out of a helicopter while on some sort of mission. But these scenes could easily be set in the "present," rather than the past, with Jason gearing up for, perhaps, a police operation. Either way, it explains why Jason is so handy with a gun.

We're then treated to various shots showing Jason and Lucia getting up to no good across Vice City, with glimpses of that steamy shower scene. The shot of Lucia wearing an ankle tag could hint at initial restrictions to exploration, as more of the world is opened up during progression through the story, but that's speculation.

This week, we learnt about GTA 6's sweat system, and there's a shot in the launch trailer that looks to show this in action. We see a man working out, and he's putting a lot of effort in. Sweat? Yep, it's all there.

"Are we gonna be okay?" Lucia asks Jason after yet more explosive shots. "We stuck together through everything," Jason replies. "Just gotta get through it."

Here's the official blurb from Rockstar on the GTA 6 launch trailer:

Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.

We also have confirmation that electronic duo Justice composed the original score for GTA 6. Indeed their track, Flower in a Hurricane, featuring fellow Grammy-winners Tame Impala and SZA along with King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, plays during the launch trailer.

It's been a busy week for GTA 6. We've got a report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , details of GTA 6’s sweat system , and confirmation GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards 2026 .

articles.title: The First 3 Die Hard Movies Are Getting the 4K Steelbook Treatment
articles.summary: Die Hard, Die Hard 2, and Die Hard With a Vengeance are getting the 4K limited-edition steelbook treatment, out in December.
articles.body:
The first three Die Hard movies are getting new limited-edition 4K steelbook releases. While the original 1988 film has been available in 4K UHD before, these new editions represent the first time the two sequels – Die Hard 2 and Die Hard with a Vengeance – will appear in the format.

These are top-tier action movies that helped boost Bruce Willis into movie star status and, frankly, they rip. They’re available for preorder now for $44.99 each ( see at Amazon ), with a release date of December 1.

Die Hard with a Vengeance - Limited-Edition Steelbook

All three movies are also Movies Anywhere eligible, meaning you can watch the included digital copies on any participating streamer, including Apple TV, Amazon Prime Video, Google Play, Fandango, and more.

It's no exaggeration to call the original Die Hard one of the best action movies ever made. Set during a company Christmas party in an otherwise deserted high-rise office building, it kicks off when a group of highly organized criminals take the partygoers hostage. What they don’t know is that out-of-town police detective John McClane (Willis) is also in the building and plans to stop them (his wife, played by Bonnie Bedilia, is one of the hostages).

This movie is as close to perfect as an action movie gets, with a script that keeps the upping the ante as the criminals discover McClane is in the building and the local police and FBI only cause further problems. The film, directed by John McTiernan (Predator, The Hunt for Red October), was so successful that it inspired a whole sub-genre of action films referred to as “Die Hard on a ____." Speed is “Die Hard on a bus,” Under Siege is “Die Hard on a boat, Air Force One is “Die Hard on a plane,” etc. This movie also introduced Alan Rickman, a gift to all humanity.

In 1990, two years after Die Hard, the sequel arrived. This movie isn’t as fondly remembered as the original, but it’s not a bad movie by any means. Directed by Renny Harlin (Cliffhanger, Deep Blue Sea), it once again takes place around Christmas, but this time in an airport. John McClane happens to be there, waiting for his wife’s plane to land, when terrorists take over the air traffic control system.

This movie revisits many of the beats of the original. Again, McClane uncovers the terrorist plot early on and has trouble convincing the local cops the threat is real. Again, official law enforcement muddles things up and the media makes things worse. But it’s a solid action film, and it performed well enough at the box office for the studio to green-light a third installment.

Die Hard with a Vengeance came out in 1995, five years after the previous entry. But it was worth the wait. John McTiernan is back in the director’s chair, and alongside Willis, the movie stars Samuel L. Jackson, fresh off Pulp Fiction, as well as the excellent, villainous Jeremy Irons.

This time around the action takes place in New York City, McClane’s home turf, as Irons’s character “Simon” threatens to detonate bombs if McClane can’t solve puzzles he’s set up for him. This movie made $366 million and was the highest-grossing film of 1995 . It still rules.

articles.title: Activision Thinks GTA 6 Will Actually Help Modern Warfare 4: 'No Offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] Are the 2 Biggest Games of the Year'
articles.summary: Activision believes GTA 6 will benefit Call of Duty rather than hinder it, with the expectation that Modern Warfare 4 and Rockstar’s behemoth will end up the two biggest games of 2026.
articles.body:
Activision believes GTA 6 will benefit Call of Duty rather than hinder it, with the expectation that Modern Warfare 4 and Rockstar’s behemoth will end up the two biggest games of 2026.

In an interview with The Game Business , Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl was asked about the prospect of GTA 6 and Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake both launching in November and creating a video game ‘Barbenheimer’ moment that might drown out Call of Duty.

However, Bahl said Call of Duty should be considered part of the conversation, insisting the increased attention on all things gaming, as well as the inevitable boost in sales of PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S that GTA 6 brings with it, will give Call of Duty a shot in the arm.

“Well, no offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] are the two biggest games of the year,” he said. “More people coming in to the dashboards, more people taking the dust off their Xbox or PlayStation and starting to play again, and loading up that experience, is going to be more eyeballs for us overall.

“At the end of the day, what makes Call of Duty last the test of time is the community and social experience. The idea of being able to play with your friends. When we look at our research and say, ‘What are the most exciting things about our games? Is it the combat or the gunplay?’ It’s actually, ‘My friends were there. Or, ‘I’m able to spend time with my friends.’ We stand on our own there, where being able to play with your friends on all different platforms, from Switch 2 this year — which is a new platform for us — all the way to PC and Xbox and PlayStation still, I think makes it a unique opportunity.”

“If more people are talking about games, if there’s more press around it, that’s going to be good for everybody, not just us,” he continued.

Activision needs Modern Warfare 4 to improve upon last year’s effort, Black Ops 7, which was a high-profile commercial disappointment for the company. Bahl admitted Activision’s strategy of releasing sub-brand sequels back-to-back (Modern Warfare 2 and 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7), simply hadn’t worked out, and fans wanted something fresh.

“It was not something that our community was looking for,” Bahl admitted. “They wanted something new and fresh. And even though there were different time settings, and different ways to play the game, and lots of new features, that tonal shift is something that they were looking for.

“So, we’ve already stated that a future title is going to be a new sub-franchise and we’ve already laid the groundwork there. But we’re really excited about what we have to offer with Modern Warfare 4, and that addresses some of that feedback we heard so loud from the community.”

Activision had already hinted that Modern Warfare 4 would bring this version of the sub-brand to an end , and Black Ops developer Treyarch has stated it’s moving on from Black Ops to work on something new. 2027, then, looks set for a brand new Call of Duty sub-brand.

“Where we go with future games, we have to innovate,” Bahl said. “What we heard from the audience is they want new or better or different. The landscape is changing right under our feet. You’re seeing new games being built overnight, and you’re seeing tastes change and how people want to play.”

Modern Warfare 4 kicks off tomorrow with the launch of campaign early access (check out the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 global release times here ). The Ocarina of Time remake comes out November 5. GTA 6, meanwhile, comes out November 19.

articles.title: SanDisk MicroSD Express Review: Super-Fast Storage for Your Switch 2
articles.summary: If you care about raw throughput when picking a microSD Express card, SanDisk’s officially-licensed microSD Express Card for Nintendo Switch 2 may be the one to beat. I’ve been testing one for the last week, and in almost every test I threw at it, it outdid IGN’s current budget pick for the best Nintendo Switch 2 microSD Express card, the Samsung P9 Express.
articles.body:
If you care about raw throughput when picking a microSD Express card, SanDisk’s officially-licensed microSD Express Card for Nintendo Switch 2 may be the one to beat. I’ve been testing one for the last week, and in almost every test I threw at it, it outdid IGN’s current budget pick for the best Nintendo Switch 2 microSD Express card , the Samsung P9 Express.

The real question is whether that’s even worth paying for. MicroSD Express cards are already very fast compared to the older microSD ones still used on every gaming handheld that’s not the Switch 2, and it’s not even close. SanDisk’s card is demonstrably faster in many ways than competing options from PNY and Samsung, but unless you’re transferring game files back and forth between it and your Switch 2, you’re really not going to notice. Faster is better, but there are other things to consider, including price.

SanDisk offers its card in 256GB, 512GB, and 1TB capacities. I’ve found 512GB to be the sweet spot, giving you three quarters of a terabyte overall when you factor in the console’s internal 256GB storage. But SanDisk’s cards cost more than similar options from PNY or Walmart’s Onn brand .

SanDisk MicroSD Express Card – Hands-On Photos

When you’re looking at the specs for a microSD Express card for Switch 2, you can safely ignore the main throughput numbers that most manufacturers like to promote. In the case of SanDisk’s card, that’s 880 MB/s reads and 650MB/s writes, which is faster than almost all the other cards I’ve tested! (The only one rated higher is the PNY one, at 890MB/s and 750MB/s, respectively.) But that number refers to the sequential read figure, and as my testing showed, is a poor reflection of actual performance during the random reads and writes.

See, video games aren’t monolithic files; they’re packages containing countless smaller files so the process of transferring them is constantly starting and stopping, slowing things significantly. How well a card performs there depends on how it handles these herky-jerky transfers.

Getting a handle on a microSD Express card’s Switch 2 throughput means timing file transfers between it and my console in docked mode. And in that, SanDisk’s card proved super capable. For instance, it reached 94 MB/s when writing Mario Kart World, currently a 22GB game (versus 21.9GB when I tested for the Samsung P9 Express before) to the card. It was actually slightly slower when it came to moving games back to the Switch 2’s internal storage, only mustering 91MB/s.

That played out the same way for every game I tested. It averaged 105MB/s when I transferred Resident Evil 4 to the card and just 80MB/s on the way back to the console, and I measured 95MB/s to the card and 85MB/s from it when moving Super Smash Bros. back and forth. The 8.9GB Donkey Kong Bananza was the fastest one; it took just over a minute to write the 8.9GB game to the card, making its throughput 122MB/s. (It averaged 88MB/s when I sent it back to internal storage.)

Despite yielding slower reads than writes, SanDisk’s card still outperformed most other cards I’ve tested in most cases. Samsung’s card put up a higher 96MB/s when I transferred Resident Evil 4 from it to my Switch 2 but otherwise ranged between about 1MB/s to 12MB/s slower on other games. The PNY card put up mostly similar read speeds, but managed closer to half the writes of the SanDisk option when it came to write speeds. That could be a difference of minutes on larger files — Mario Kart World took over seven minutes to write to PNY’s card, something that only took about four minutes with SanDisk’s. Basically, if you find yourself shuffling games on and off your Switch 2, the SanDisk microSD Express card could save you real time.

Things equalize where it’s most important: actual loading times for games. Measuring these, I found that the SanDisk card looked almost exactly the same as both the PNY and Samsung cards I tested before. Donkey Kong Bananza took 21 seconds to go from choosing it on the Switch 2’s home screen to its title screen, just like those cards. Mario Kart World averaged 19.4 seconds, or a tenth of a second behind the PNY card and about two seconds faster than the Samsung P9. It got me into The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom nearly a full second faster, at 8.5 seconds, than either of those cards, though.

It’s clear that SanDisk’s officially-licensed Switch 2 card is at least as good as the other high-performing cards on the market, so you won’t be disappointed. It’s still slower than loading games from the Switch 2’s internal storage for the most part, but the difference is negligible – most games only load a fraction of a second faster from the Switch 2 itself than from microSD Express.

Wes is a freelance writer (Freelance Wes, they call him) who has covered technology, gaming, and entertainment steadily since 2020 at Gizmodo, Tom's Hardware, Hardcore Gamer, and most recently, The Verge. Inside of him there are two wolves: one that thinks it wouldn't be so bad to start collecting game consoles again, and the other who also thinks this, but more strongly.

articles.title: The New Street Fighter Movie Is Dumber Than a Box of Rocks, But It Can Also Be Pretty Fun!
articles.summary: Review: Street Fighter benefits from a very enthusiastic cast and an anarchic spirit, but Kitao Sakurai’s adaptation of the Capcom games struggles to focus all that energy into a well-told story.
articles.body:
Street Fighter is in theaters on October 16.

There’s an infectious and celebratory energy coursing through Kitao Sakurai’s Street Fighter at every turn… Psycho Power, you could say. And “Psycho Power” is an apt metaphysical concept to have so front-and-center of the movie’s plot, because as Capcom’s roster of colorful and strange lowercase “c” combatants strut their stuff and pull off their special moves in hyperkinetic fashion, the movie increasingly feels disconnected from any sense of reality, even its own. Is that really a problem when you’ve got martial arts warriors and demons throwing fireballs, green monsters with Jason Momoa’s face rolling around, or Eric Andre screaming through a bullhorn at the top of his lungs? As it turns out, yes. But, as you quickly learn while watching it, Street Fighter never lets good sense get in the way of a good time.

Street Fighter gets off to a stylish start with a wonderfully executed anime prologue that sets up the divide between protagonists Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken (Noah Centineo), martial artists who’d grown to be best friends while training under their master Gouken (Don Lee). As Ryu fades into obscurity, Ken becomes a pop culture mainstay who can never quite shake the idea that his former friend was the better fighter after Ryu demonstrates an ability to harness “Hado power.” That mystical energy from the spirit realm is only able to be channeled by the greatest warriors, and Sakurai and co-writer T.J. Fixman devote about as many words in their script to explaining it as are included in this very sentence.

More necessary to the plot is how important this ability is to M. Bison (David Dastmalchian), the sadistic leader of the Shadaloo crime organization who stages a tournament of the world’s greatest fighters in hopes of sapping enough Hado power (or Psycho Power, as it’s called around Bison’s office) for him to unlock special moves of his very own. Street Fighter makes a bet that scant few in its audience are going to give two rips about how well-justified its melting pot of characters, magic abilities, and cultural influences winds up, with Sakurai seeming far more intent on representing the franchise as broadly as possible at the cost of telling a deeper story.

The fast and loose nature of the adaptation’s storytelling relies heavily on expected genre tropes for both Ryu and Ken, and that effort falls frustratingly short of how good both Andrew Koji and Noah Centineo are in their respective roles. Between the two, Centineo’s Ken gets more latitude to demonstrate how his attention-starved tenure in Ryu’s shadow has affected him, and Centineo’s restlessness gives Ken a fun “little brother” energy that feels like it goes a lot further to propping up his underdog status within the story than the actual writing of the character does. Ken’s reasons for staying locked into the tournament are never quite clear: Is he here to prove himself against Ryu? To honor his master? To save himself from more MTV Spring Break appearances? To save the world ? Maybe for supporting characters, those reasons are less important. But as one of the two leads and certainly the one with more time in the spotlight, Ken’s motivation could have used a lot more focus, which would’ve allowed for his struggles later in the movie to hit home with the emotional weight the finale seems to be making space for.

Ryu’s arc has the inverse problem, with a poorly maintained throughline about his struggle with a dark power hiding just under the surface of his otherwise peaceful demeanor. He’s reluctant to engage with the tournament as a result, with that struggle embodied by Roman Reigns’ demonic Akuma, the games character which Street Fighter goes furthest out of its way to justify bringing into the fold here. As great as the Ryu/Ken anime scenes look, Sakurai flashes back to them more and more, which becomes a distracting crutch the movie uses to double back on itself and explain Akuma’s significance to Ryu and Ken’s early days.

It’s a shame, as Andrew Koji is quite compelling as Ryu and does great work keeping the character’s stoicism from drifting into feeling wooden, as often happens with action leads. With how cartoonishly emotive the other characters are, Ryu’s calm is a welcome contrast to whatever weirdo he’s paired up with in any given scene. Perhaps unsurprisingly, Ryu’s intense focus is best juxtaposed against Ken’s manic enthusiasm, and Koji and Centineo are each at their best when bickering with each other. An early fight between the two in a hotel room synthesizes that dynamic best in both performance and action, as Ryu’s one-upsmanship in the duel drives Ken increasingly up a wall. That relatively straightforward fight, and the precise nature of how the camera chases the choreography to accentuate comedic beats, is a bit of an outlier for Street Fighter because the rest of the fights are textbook examples of unchecked maximalism.

Street Fighter never lets too long go by without a brawl breaking out. Whether or not those brawls have any good reason to be happening, the movie certainly kicks into a higher gear when fists are flying, even if the tournament that acts as the backbone of the movie’s second half is pretty much an afterthought. The action blends Hong Kong, anime, and ’80s/’90s movie influences that alternatingly emphasize tight fight choreography and epic hero moments. In that way, ironically, that leaves Scott Pilgrim vs. The World’s video game-inspired action as the closest cinematic relative to Street Fighter’s, a similarity that also makes its way into how the movie’s comedic bent leaves that action needing to function as an engine for both adrenaline and laughs. Sakurai opts for a scattershot approach here, with a tendency to pack action scenes so full with individual gags that often there’s not enough time to fully appreciate them before he’s moving on to the next one. The action is very well-performed by the stunt team and those in the cast like Andrew Koji who are capable of handling the more complicated sequences themselves, but the plot does leave Street Fighter relying more on VFX embellishments to that action as it goes, which add very little to how viscerally it all lands.

The movie’s wide scope does lead to a pretty strong showing from the games’ deep bench of fighters, and the flavor each of their personalities bring to this whacked-out stew are the undeniable highlight of the movie. Through its first half, Street Fighter bends over backwards to introduce game characters like Chun-Li (Callina Liang), Guile (Cody Rhodes), Vega (Orville Peck), Dhalsim (Vidyut Jammwal), and Cammy (Mel Jarnson) and to keep them in the mix as the tournament begins in MetroLao City. These characters’ personal reasons for accepting their invitations become wholly irrelevant after they’re in the door, but Street Fighter is no weaker for that. With no responsibilities to the plot, these fighters are given license to be as bizarre and funny as their individual performers can sustain, and the characters that leave a mark really leave a mark.

Andrew Schulz’s Dan Hibiki, Ken’s replacement best friend after Ryu disappears, is the big surprise on that front. As Ken’s agent, Dan begins the story looking like a money-hungry leech, but his genuine care for his buddy actually becomes one of the few emotional hooks that the movie’s got by the end, and Schulz plays being out of his depth around people who could rock his shit to frequently funny effect. Another comedian who sees big success throughout Street Fighter is Eric Andre, whose emcee Don Sauvage is essentially just a thinly veiled spin on his own signature chaos energy.

From the moment Cody Rhodes’ Guile enters (hair first, of course) to the tune of his absolutely rocking theme song, the strength of his all-American charisma and consistent ability to nail punchlines are let down only by the relatively brief amount of screentime he gets. Others — like Balrog or Zangief — are glorified cameos that at least each add a unique energy to their scenes. Jason Momoa’s Blanka certainly falls into this camp: He’s barely involved, but dang it if the freakish CGI and “Hulked on Phonics” speech pattern that define him don’t leave you leaning in with amused bewilderment by the time he rolls out of the movie. David Dastmalchian’s M. Bison is another reliable source of amusing bewilderment that Street Fighter draws on to great effect: Bison’s relationship to power and just how… gratified he becomes as he creeps closer and closer to attaining it is a surprisingly off-kilter approach to the imposing dictator, and one that Dastmalchian never blinks in the face of.

These characters really exemplify the importance of good casting, as each performer brings inherent strengths to the roles which make up a lot of ground for how underwritten many of them are. That lack of definition does backfire with the most prominent female characters: Callina Liang’s Chun-Li and Mel Jarnson’s Cammy are certainly pretty high up on the list of historically overly sexualized video game characters, a fact Street Fighter doesn’t have an intelligent enough take on to poke fun at without just perpetuating it further. But whether it’s a character rooted in strong cinematic archetypes like Guile or unfortunate ones like Chun-Li, all of the performers wholeheartedly embrace the movie’s ridiculous tone and keep it afloat when the writing lets them down. Street Fighter’s 1990s setting is supposed to be another source of campy energy for the movie, but Sakurai never quite figures out how to effectively channel that nostalgia — little of the production design feels that demonstrative of the period, leaving the way-too-frequent needle drops (including one that released on the whole other end of the decade in which the movie’s set) doing all the heavy lifting on that score.

articles.title: Brewers-Dodgers NLCS Game 1 is most-watched LCS game since 2005
articles.summary: More than 10.7 million viewers tuned in to watch the Brewers beat the Dodgers 2-1 in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series.
articles.body:
More than 10.7 million viewers tuned in to watch the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-1 in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series, according to Fox Sports.

That's enough to make it the most-watched LCS Game 1 on any network since 2005 and the most-watched LCS game overall on any network since 2010, Fox Sports said.

Game 1 was played Sunday night, Oct. 11 at American Family Field in Milwaukee. The pivotal moment came in the bottom of the fifth inning, when an RBI single by right fielder Luis Lara put the Brewers ahead by a run.

Here's more about the television audience for Game 1 of the NLCS.

How does the NLCS Game 1 broadcast compare to last postseason?

The television audience for NLCS Game 1 between the Brewers and the Dodgers was more than twice the size it was for Game 1 of the American League Championship Series in 2025, when about 5.2 million viewers tuned in to Fox to see the Seattle Mariners defeated the Toronto Blue Jays .

What was the peak number of viewers for Brewers vs. Dodgers in NLCS Game 1?

The telecast had about 12.4 million viewers on Fox from 7 to 7:15 p.m. CT, just as the game began with Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound.

Game 4 of the NLCS is scheduled for 7 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 15 , with the Brewers one win away from securing a spot in the World Series.

If necessary, Game 5 would be played at 8 p.m. Friday, Oct. 16 at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Zendaya and Alex 'Ex Machina' Garland Team up for New Sci-Fi Movie
articles.summary: It's just been announced that Dune and Spider-Man star Zendaya is working on a science fiction project with Ex Machina director Alex Garland.
articles.body:
It's just been announced that Dune and Spider-Man star Zendaya is working on a science fiction project with Ex Machina director Alex Garland. The unnamed project will be released by A24, an entertainment company that has made a name for itself with weird and wonderful projects.

According to Variety , the plot is also secret for now, but Garland's previous science fiction works have focused on revealing the good and bad in human nature through futuristic ideas like clones, androids, and quantum computing. Last year it was confirmed that one of Garland's current projects is writing and directing an Elden Ring adaptation , also with A24.

"Sci-fi allows really, really big subject matter without having to feel embarrassed about it, and a lot of other genres, including, by the way, straight adult drama, is sometimes really embarrassed of big ideas," he said of his attraction to the genre in an interview last year.

"Sci-fi just says, 'Do whatever you want. The bigger the idea, the better. Bring it on.'"

Zendaya's upcoming movies include Dune: Part Three, set for release on December 18, the Ronnie Spector biopic Be My Baby, and she's lent her voice to the new Shrek movie.

She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. articles.title: CD Projekt Has Officially Begun Work on Project Hadar, but It's Not in Pre-Production Yet
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red, the Polish developer best known for its amazing RPG series The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077, has officially finished imagining up a new world for us to play in. The “world vision” stage for its new IP, Project Hadar, has been completed and work has officially begun on turning those concepts into a video game.
articles.body:
CD Projekt Red, the Polish developer best known for its amazing RPG series The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077 , has officially finished imagining up a new world for us to play in. The “world vision” stage for its new IP, Project Hadar, has been completed and work has officially begun on turning those concepts into a video game.

"This has been our biggest undertaking to date, taking us several years, but at this point we can say we have a coherent vision for this world and its key elements,” said Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski . “The team has begun work on the game, although it's not yet in pre-production.”

In September, CD Projekt Red said it was staffing up for Project Hadar, with a team over 30 strong with plans "to hire more, up to 50 developers by the end of this year. But what is it? In June, a new job advert teased what to expect , calling for an engineering director who would help “push the envelope for the next, immersive game in the Hadar world, creating an emotional, open-world experience that will stay with gamers.” Open-world confirmed!

Every CD Projekt Red Game In Development

CD Projekt Red is of course currently hard at work making The Witcher 4, which is the next game on the studio’s slate due out 2028. Before that, though, a third major expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, titled Songs of the Past, is scheduled for release next year. Developed by Fool’s Theory, a team of former CD Projekt developers, the expansion aims to bridge the gap between The Witcher 3 and the next game in the series, starring Geralt’s adopted daughter, Ciri.

After that comes Cyberpunk 2, the follow-up to Cyberpunk 2077. And let's not forget that CD Projekt intends to release the new The Witcher 3 trilogy in the space of six years. Assuming CD Projekt hits 2028 for The Witcher 4, and the company sticks to its ambitious release strategy for this new The Witcher trilogy , we could see The Witcher 5 in 2031 and The Witcher 6 in 2034. Where Hadar fits in with all that is anyone's guess.

We know nothing about Project Hadar’s world or setting, but it’ll be cool to see what the wonderful minds at CDPR think up — especially as it’ll be designed first and foremost to support a sprawling RPG. I do selfishly wish CDPR would do one more license though. Give us a good Game of Thrones video game. Please. You could call it Project Hodor.

The next series of the anime based on CDPR and Pondsmith’s shared world is coming to Netflix on October 20. You can check out our interview with the creator of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 for the lowdown.

Elsewhere in CD Project Land, The Witcher 3 just got a remaster on consoles and PC, which saw the iconic RPG get a makeover to tide people over until the expansion. There were some issues with the new visuals, particularly heavy bloom in The Witcher 3 remaster , but CDPR fixed its prized goose sharpish.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Episode 3 Hints at the Return of the 'My Cabbages!' Guy
articles.body:
With the release of Avatar: Seven Havens, I decided to cave and grab a Paramount+ subscription just to watch it. After checking out the first three episodes , I can honestly say I'm hooked. With the series creators returning on the project, it feels like quintessential ATLA.

My newfound subscription also granted me access to the recent Avatar Aang movie , which I also loved. But there's one element of that movie that stood out to me: the inclusion of the "My cabbages!" guy. It's a long-running joke in the series that even made it's way into The Legend of Korra via the cabbage merchant's son, who ran Cabbage Corp in Republic City.

So as I started watching Seven Havens, one question on my mind was whether or not the cabbage joke could actually get referenced in this series. The first few episodes show off a dusty, post-apocalyptic world that doesn't immediately seem like it's conducive to cabbage farming. Most of the foods you see in the first few episodes are brown, and the foliage seems oddly geometric as the characters make their way throughout the environment. But there is one scene in Episode 3 that points to the possibility of a cabbage man.

Without going into any spoilers about the episode or the series so far, I wanted to hone in on the above specific screenshot from Episode 3 of the show. Specifically, this is the first time we see something even remotely cabbage-like. While this does appear to be some form of cauliflower here, its existence suggests that it is possible to grow cabbages in this world. Both cauliflower and cabbage are cruciferous vegetables that share very similar growing conditions. Cabbage is actually easier to grow than cauliflower.

So now that we know that cabbages do probably exist in this new environment, it seems all but inevitable that we'll see some sort of reference to the "My cabbages!" gag later in the series. I'd be very surprised if the creators were to choose this particular series to remove a fan-favorite ongoing reference. The question is just how connected the reference will be to the original cabbage merchant.

In The Legend of Korra, the owner of Cabbage Corp was Lau Gan-Lan , who had taken over the business from his father, the original cabbage merchant. There is no reference in that series that Lau Gan-Lan has any sort of descendent, but it seems likely that he'd want to leave his cabbage empire to somebody. It's clear in Avatar: Seven Havens so far that something horrible happened to destroy the world we knew at the end of Korra's time as Avatar, something which likely put an end to Cabbage Corp. But that doesn't mean the family business didn't continue.

There are still 10 episodes left in the season, so there's plenty of time to set up some solid cabbage lore before the finale. This innocuous cauliflower stand may not be the strongest indicator that we'll get that reference, but it's enough for me to believe it will happen.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: A Massive Decompilation Community Is Shutting Down, Thanks to the Deluge of AI Decomps and Ports
articles.summary: If you've been on gaming Twitter at all over the last month, you're probably aware of a massive wave of people using AI to rapidly decompile, port and remix games. Well, that wave of AI decomps has forced a massive decompilation community to sunset.
articles.body:
If you've been on gaming Twitter at all over the last month, you're probably aware of the massive wave of people using AI to rapidly decompile, port, and remix games. That wave of AI decomps has forced a massive decompilation community to sunset.

In a blog post, admin @encounter from decomp.dev , a community repository for people to track decompilation posts, cites a wave of bad actors who are using AI to essentially steal the hard work of programmers working on existing decompilation projects.

The act of decompiling games itself isn't new, and people have been taking games and trying to decompile them down to the source code for years. But what was once a herculean task requiring coding expertise can now be done with little effort thanks to new AI models like GPT 6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.

The blog post doesn't blame the models themselves for the surge of vibe-coded decompilations and ports, but rather claims that bad actors are taking existing projects and then using AI to rush them to completion. While there might be some developers who are open to people with a Claude subscription using their work to create, say, a browser port of Halo , that should be up to each developer.

The post says, "Every project works differently: some may not want to use AI for legal or ethical reasons, and others may be okay with AI, or use AI themselves, but do not want drive-by contributions from folks who have put no effort into making sure the contributions are good. The bottom line is that these kinds of hostile forks put little to no effort into meaningfully contributing to existing projects, tearing apart our community fabric."

As for the ports themselves, the blog claims that people are taking the code from hobbyists and forcing a barely functioning port out of them. "While community members put in the effort to decompile a game, opportunists have frequently raced to release a half-baked, barely-functional port from it," @encounter writes.

The blog post also mentions that this recent wave of AI decomps, recomps, and ports is muddying the waters of what the decomp community is trying to do. A lot of classical decomps are done out of the love of games and a desire to know how they work, but this trend of using AI to brute force working PC ports has caused a lot of people to rush into communities like decomp.dev looking for simple ways to create easy PC ports of games.

As for decomp.dev itself, the website will still exist, and users can use it to track existing projects, but @encounter is taking down the main index and disabling new projects.

Unfortunately, when it comes to Opus 5.5, Astra 6, and decomps, the cat is out of the bag, and it's unlikely that one decomp repository going offline is going to meaningfully stop this trend. We've seen everything from making Minecraft playable on X/Twitter to modders shoving Minecraft and Elden Ring together . There have also been a lot of browser ports, with games like Halo: Combat Evolved and Grand Theft Auto 5 being briefly playable on Chrome before those games' respective publishers predictibly brought them crashing down.

Either way, it's a shame to see a community built out of the love of programming essentially die off because a bunch of people with Claude subscriptions are using game developers' work as a starting point and finishing it with AI.

articles.title: The Batman Part II Production Pause Is Not Permanent, DC Studios Confirms
articles.summary: The show must go on. DC Studios co-CEO and co-chairman Peter Safran addressed the production stoppage on The Batman: Part II in a new interview with IGN.
articles.body:
The show must go on. DC Studios co-CEO and co-chairman Peter Safran addressed the production stoppage on The Batman: Part II in a new interview with IGN.

Filming of The Batman: Part II had been underway in the UK until it was halted earlier this month so that director Matt Reeves could see to a "family matter."

"Production on The Batman Part II has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” Warner Bros. stated at the time. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.”

Here’s my exact exchange with Safran from our chat this past Monday.

IGN: I want to be very delicate about how I ask this. Is there any scenario where Batman: Part II doesn't start filming again?

Whether that means filming will resume at some point under Reeves’ direction or if a replacement will take over the directing reins remains to be seen.

Elsewhere in our full interview with him, Safran said of the film, “Batman: Part II, everybody's aware of the issues we're having right now, but, what we've seen so far of the shoot, it looked absolutely fantastic and Matt Reeves is a supremely talented filmmaker.”

A sequel to Reeves’ 2022 film, The Batman: Part II is going in “another totally different direction” than its predecessor, according to star Robert Pattinson.

Speculation about Part II’s plot and characters has been rampant online, with everyone from the Court of Owls to Mister Freeze and Two-Face rumored to factor into its story.

Photos and videos from the Glasgow set were all over social media before production was temporarily shut down, including a closer look at Batman’s updated Arkham-style batsuit and a chase sequence between Batman and the Gotham City Police . The Batmobile itself appears in pretty bad shape after some barrel rolls in some of the set photos.

It’s unclear right now if The Batman Part II’s release date will be pushed again . It’s currently scheduled to open in theaters on February 18, 2028.

articles.title: LEGO Venetian Neighborhood Set Is Coming in November
articles.summary: LEGO has announced a gorgeous Venetian Neighborhood set that releases in November, but it's not cheap at $550.
articles.body:
LEGO has announced a new 5,682-piece set called LEGO Icons Venetian Neighborhood. It’s an intricate set depicting several Italian buildings situated on a canal, with a bridge connecting them. It’s a well populated Venice scene, as it includes 17 minifigures.

The price fits the high piece count; it costs $549.99 and is scheduled to release November 1 for LEGO Insiders (you can sign up here for free) or November 4 for everyone else. You can view the listing here , but preorders are not available.

It’s a lovely set that includes, according to the official description, a “luxury villa, an artisan glassblowing workshop and astronomical clock tower.” The buildings are built in a modular way that lets you remove roofs and entire floors to see the detailed interiors. In addition, the set can be separated into two distinct sections to create alternate display layouts, keeping things fresh.

Also included is a long gondola that fits neatly under the arched bridge. The 17 minifigures populating the neighborhood include gondoliers, musicians, tourists, and two carnival-goers dressed in costumes and masks. Also included is a 3D-printed street piano piece (you can see a close-up of it in the slideshow below).

Buying the set at the LEGO Store will also get you the LEGO Icons Venetian Water Taxi set (40898) as a free Gift With Purchase. It’s a 322-piece set containing a water taxi and a dock setting, plus captain and tourist minifigures, as well as two pigeon figures.

LEGO Venetian Neighborhood is the latest announcement in the LEGO Icons theme, which features somewhat intricate sets intended for adults or advanced builders. These sets are intended for display rather than play, and consist of things like impressive buildings, vehicles, and classic pop culture, well, icons. It’s a pretty loose theme as these things go, seeing as it fits everything from the massive LEGO Titanic set to a set based on Toothless from How to Train Your Dragon. You can see all the current LEGO Icons sets here .

LEGO releases tend to peter out toward the end of the year, and that appears to be the case in 2026 as well. Including this one, only four sets have been announced for November, with a grand total of zero sets announced for December. However, we can expect a big new LEGO set to release on Black Friday, as is tradition. That set has yet to be announced.

For more, check out our full list of upcoming LEGO sets , complete with release dates, set numbers, pricing, and links to preorder where available.

It’s little surprise, then, that Nikki is the third most-searched Halloween costume this year on Google, as told by the platform’s ‘Frightgeist’ page.
